title: Utility Commands (util time-ms, util uuid, util time-now)
description: Implement three utility commands: util time-ms outputs the current UTC time as a Unix millisecond timestamp; util uuid generates a random UUID v4; util time-now outputs the current India Standard Time (GMT+5:30) formatted as DD/MM/YY HH:mm:ss.fff (24-hour with milliseconds). All are stateless with no account, auth, or network dependencies.
prerequisiteState: Stories 1 and 2 complete. IOutputWriter, ZapiCliException, GlobalSettings, and Program.cs CommandApp all exist. No account or auth infrastructure required.
goal: zapi-cli util time-ms outputs {"ts": <unix ms timestamp>}, zapi-cli util uuid outputs {"uuid": "<uuid v4>"}, and zapi-cli util time-now outputs {"now": "DD/MM/YY HH:mm:ss.fff"} (IST, 24-hour with milliseconds) on stdout as plain JSON. All commands exit 0.
scope: Create src/ZapiCli/Commands/UtilCommands.cs with three command classes.
UtilTimeMsCommand extends AsyncCommand<UtilTimeMsSettings>: call DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds(); WriteJson(new { ts = timestampMs }). Exit 0.
UtilUuidCommand extends AsyncCommand<UtilUuidSettings>: call Guid.NewGuid().ToString(); WriteJson(new { uuid = guidString }). Exit 0.

UtilTimeNowCommand extends AsyncCommand<UtilTimeNowSettings>: convert UtcNow to IST using a fixed +05:30 offset via TimeZoneInfo.CreateCustomTimeZone; format as 'dd/MM/yy HH:mm:ss.fff' (24-hour with milliseconds); WriteJson(new { now = formattedString }). Exit 0.
Register all three commands under the 'util' branch in Program.cs CommandApp.

Unit tests: UtilTimeMsCommand returns a long > 0 in the ts field; the value is within 5 seconds of DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds(); UtilUuidCommand returns a non-empty string in the uuid field that parses as a valid Guid; UtilTimeNowCommand returns a non-empty string in the now field that matches the pattern dd/MM/yy hh:mm:ss tt and is within 2 seconds of the expected IST time.
acceptanceCriteria: dotnet build succeeds with 0 errors and 0 warnings
zapi-cli util time-ms outputs {"ts": <number>} on stdout, number is a positive long, exit 0
zapi-cli util uuid outputs {"uuid": "<xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx>"} on stdout, exit 0
zapi-cli util time-now outputs {"now": "DD/MM/YY HH:mm:ss.fff"} in IST (GMT+5:30, 24-hour with milliseconds), exit 0
util time-now uses a fixed +05:30 offset (no OS timezone database dependency)
Neither command touches accounts.json, keychain, or network
All commands respect --no-input without any different behaviour (they are always non-interactive)
contextForAgent: Three simple stateless utility commands. Use Guid.NewGuid().ToString() for UUID v4. Use DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds() for the Unix ms timestamp. For time-now, use TimeZoneInfo.CreateCustomTimeZone to create a fixed IST offset of +05:30 — this avoids OS timezone database dependency (cross-platform safe). Format with 'dd/MM/yy hh:mm:ss tt' (C# format string). All output via IOutputWriter.WriteJson. Register with the correct Spectre command tree: zapi-cli util time-ms, zapi-cli util uuid, and zapi-cli util time-now.
